On 9/26/12 3:15 PM, Richard McElreath wrote:
The extract method in rstan has been frustrating me, as it appears to get rapidly slower as the @sim results get bigger
in the stanfit object. I noticed this, because I fit a series of models in Stan and then went about simulating
predictions from each. The computations bogged down in the larger models, and some investigation revealed the delay was
happening inside rstan::extract.

I ended up writing my own faster extract function (see below), so worked around the problem. But if it's easy to fix it,
might be worth adding to the to-do list.

Here's my special-purpose extract that performs well (but is not as flexible as extract), along with some system.time
results, to see how big the delay can be.

|
fastx <- function( object , par ) {
     begin <- attr(object@sim[[1]][[1]],"args")$warmup + 1
     end <- attr(object@sim[[1]][[1]],"args")$iter
     object@sim[[1]][[1]][[ par ]][begin:end]
}
|

Timed below for extracting 5000 non-warmup samples from a single chain, for a single parameter. The model has a few
thousands parameters, so a big @sim object.

 > system.time( mean( fastx( fit , "mu[1]" ) ) )

    user  system elapsed

   0.004   0.001   0.004

 >

 > system.time( mean( extract( fit , "mu[1]" , inc_warmup=FALSE ) ) )

    user  system elapsed

   0.411   0.293   1.229
